mn126:7.2: “Sir, I robed up in the morning and, taking my bowl and robe, went to the home of Prince Jayasena, where I sat down on the seat spread out.
mn126:7.3: Then, sir, Jayasena approached me and exchanged greetings with me.
mn126:7.4: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to me:
mn126:7.5: ‘Worthy Bhūmija, there are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:
mn126:7.6: If you make a wish and lead the spiritual life, you can’t win the fruit.
mn126:7.7: If you don’t make a wish …
mn126:7.8: If you both make a wish and don’t make a wish and lead the spiritual life, you can’t win the fruit.
mn126:7.9: If you neither make a wish nor don’t make a wish and lead the spiritual life, you can’t win the fruit.’
mn126:7.10: ‘What does the worthy Bhūmija’s Teacher say about this? How does he explain it?’
mn126:7.11: When he said this, sir, I said to Prince Jayasena,
mn126:7.12: ‘I haven’t heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha.
mn126:7.13: But it’s possible that he might explain it like this:
mn126:7.14: If you lead the spiritual life irrationally, you can’t win the fruit, regardless of whether you make a wish,
mn126:7.16: you both do and do not make a wish,
mn126:7.17: or you neither do nor don’t make a wish.
mn126:7.18: But if you lead the spiritual life rationally, you can win the fruit, regardless of whether you make a wish,
mn126:7.20: you both do and do not make a wish …
mn126:7.21: or you neither do nor don’t make a wish.
mn126:7.22: I haven’t heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha.
mn126:7.23: But it’s possible that he might explain it like that.’
mn126:7.24: ‘If that’s what your teacher says, worthy Bhūmija, he clearly stands head and shoulders above all the various other ascetics and brahmins.’
